GAME ATLAS · Built for the curious chess mind.A reproducible, open-source experiment.
THE MAP IS NOT THE TERRITORY

A way to explore.
Not a verdict on style.

The strategic map describes the target player’s positions and decisions, starting after 12 opening plies and ending at ply 120. It pools three chronological segments of each game.

Its 288 dimensions cover piece placement, pawn structure, mobility and control, king safety, material balance, and move choices. Features are standardized, clipped, weighted by block, and normalized. Names and results are never inputs.

We use PCA followed by t-SNE to draw the map. Recommendations use distance in the full fingerprint space, not distance on your screen. Cluster sizes and gaps in a t-SNE map are not reliable measures of strategic differences.

The selector also exposes the original 12-statistic PCA baseline. Neither representation is a trained neural model. The strategic fingerprint has more chess information, but its ability to capture style still needs evaluation.

Player colors identify the source collection and target perspective. A shared game appears once. The collection is a deterministic sample of real PGNs; no account or server-side processing is needed.
